subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: What liveness contract should WebChat enforce when a persisted Codex native thread is oversized or cannot begin a turn after `chat.send`?
rationale: Current main contains plausible mitigations, but choosing between fail-fast, forced rotation, delayed ACK semantics, and health/doctor recovery changes user-visible behavior and Codex boundary ownership.

options.title: Require visible liveness before success
options.body: Treat `started` as valid only when dispatch reaches a runnable Codex thread, otherwise force-rotate when safe or report a visible/auditable failure.

options.title: Prove current main sufficient
options.body: Keep the implementation unchanged only if a current-main live or fixture replay of the oversized persisted thread proves sends reach `turn/start` or a visible error reliably.

options.title: Split recovery from send semantics
options.body: Leave non-blocking `chat.send` semantics intact but add explicit health/doctor recovery for Codex native thread stalls before closing this issue.

recommendation.title: Require visible liveness before success
recommendation.body: Treat `started` as valid only when dispatch reaches a runnable Codex thread, otherwise force-rotate when safe or report a visible/auditable failure.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the most recent merged overflow-rotation implementation on the affected Codex app-server boundary.
